source.title: Listen and Chant Before You Read: The Ladder of Beauty in LM Pre-Training

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies music pre-pre-training and transfer, and discusses how auxiliary-data volume interacts with model capacity. It does not test the stated power laws, extrapolation, fixed-compute allocation, or fit dependence.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Hoffmann et al. and reports its own model-size and auxiliary-music-data-volume sweeps. Those results concern WikiText validation perplexity after transfer, not power-law fits to held-out pretraining loss or a fixed-compute parameter/token optimum. The related sweep results are recorded under fits_no_version; none of the listed claim versions is tested.
record.test_reason: The study tests music→poetry→prose pre-pre-training on tiny Transformers (33K–400K params) and reports WikiText validation perplexity after a fixed 3-epoch horizon. It fits no power law, extrapolates nothing, and runs no fixed-compute allocation. Its only sweeps are 3 model widths and 3 auxiliary-data volumes of music transfer data, which is a different construct from held-out pretraining loss scaling. It cites Hoffmann et al. only in passing. No claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. It should add the following. The pipeline gives −17.5% perplexity at d=16 over 5 seeds (p<0.001). It beats a compute-matched 5-epoch baseline by 5.0%. A 5.5% gap persists at plateau at d=64 over 5 seeds (p=0.017). Real music matches synthetic transfer with one-third the data. The authors stress that all results are at small scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses staged auxiliary music and poetry pretraining followed by prose training, with validation-perplexity sweeps; it does not fit the original scaling-law models or perform fixed-compute allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported preferred MAESTRO data volume changes across model sizes: 12,000 chunks is better at d = 16, while 36,000 chunks is better at d = 32 and d = 64.

fits_no_version.finding: For MAESTRO pre-pre-training, the auxiliary data volume giving better WikiText transfer shifts with model width. 36k-vs-12k advantage: −3.1% at d=16, +3.3% at d=32, +6.1% at d=64 (single seed). Synthetic music improves monotonically with volume at d=16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In music→language transfer, the beneficial volume of auxiliary pre-pre-training data grows with model capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a poetry stage after MAESTRO-36k further lowers epoch-2 WikiText perplexity at d=32 (215.0→196.3, single seed).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A poetry stage after music pre-pre-training adds transfer benefit in small Transformers.

record.problems: The authors state that the experiments reach at most d = 64 (approximately 400K parameters), use a narrow English and Western-classical-piano setting, and report no downstream-task evaluation. Phase 1 and Phase 3 scaling experiments use a single seed; the paper notes that multi-seed replication of the scaling results would strengthen the conclusions.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included. The convergence tests and compute-matched comparison concern the transfer pipeline rather than the scaling-law claims; cited findings from other work were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute. Only 3 widths (33K–400K) evaluated after a fixed 3-epoch horizon.
No fixed-compute sweep or parameter/token optimum. The compute-matched control compares pipelines, not allocations.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.
Music is used only as an auxiliary transfer stage. No power-law form is tested for music modelling or for transfer.
No downstream tasks; the authors state they report only perplexity.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: Phases 2, 4.6 and the compute-matched control are omitted from the rows. These results concern pipeline transfer, not any scaling-law version, so their omission does not affect the verdicts. The Hoffmann et al. citation is used only in contrast: "more data is almost always beneficial" for language pretraining.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit to held-out pretraining loss across parameters, tokens, or compute; the reported metric is WikiText validation perplexity after transfer.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
The study does not compare depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Music is used as an auxiliary pre-pre-training stage, but the study does not test whether a power-law form holds in that or other regimes.
No downstream task performance is measured or predicted; the study reports language-model validation perplexity.
The study does not compare scaling-law fitting choices or estimate exponents or a compute-optimal split.

relation.reason: Section 5.5 contrasts capacity-dependent auxiliary-data saturation with language-pretraining data benefits, citing Hoffmann et al.; the experiments neither test nor operationally use the catalog's scaling laws.

tranche.reason: The study measures auxiliary music/poetry transfer and its interaction with model capacity. It tests no specified power-law form, extrapolation, stable compute-optimal powers, architecture invariance, downstream-task predictability, or fitting dependence.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical cells and conditions match Tables 5, 8 and 9; Phases 1 and 3 use seed 42 and a 10% WikiText-103 subsample. Main rows report the study's method performance and belong outside claim-evidence rows; their transfer benefits do not establish any scaling_laws version.
